## Lisbon Apartment Fit for Remote Work

A strong match for your priorities is **Avenidas Novas**: it fits the budget exactly, has **fiber internet**, and is generally one of the better areas for transit and coworking access. If you want the best value on price, **Arroios** is the cheaper fallback, but it comes with more uncertainty.

## Ranked Apartment Comparison

| Rank | Area | Rent | Size | Internet | Quiet / Transit / Coworking Fit | Verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Avenidas Novas | €1,600 | 55 m² | Fiber | Good quiet-to-central balance; strong transit and coworking access | **Best overall fit** |
| 2 | Campo de Ourique | €1,700 | 50 m² | 300 Mbps | Quiet and comfortable, but over budget | **Best quality, too expensive** |
| 3 | Arroios | €1,350 | 48 m² | Fiber | Good value and central access, but mixed reviews reduce confidence | **Best value if you can verify the building** |
| 4 | Alfama | €1,450 | 42 m² | 20 Mbps | Charming but older, smaller, and internet is a weak point | **Not ideal for remote work** |

## Best Match by Option

### 1) Avenidas Novas — Best Overall
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Why it wins:** exact budget match, **55 m²** is the most usable size, and **fiber internet** supports video calls and heavy work.
- **Remote-work fit:** strong access to metro and coworking spots without the noise and tourist traffic of more historic neighborhoods.
- **Trade-off:** you’re paying the full budget, so there’s less room for utilities or upgrades.

### 2) Arroios — Best Value
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-euro.svg
- **Why it stands out:** **€1,350** leaves room in your budget, and fiber is a major plus.
- **Remote-work fit:** central enough for transit and coworking, usually practical for daily life.
- **Trade-off:** “mixed reviews” is a real warning sign; building quality, street noise, or management may vary a lot.

### 3) Campo de Ourique — Best Quality, Over Budget
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/star.svg
- **Why it appeals:** likely the most comfortable-feeling option, with **300 Mbps** internet and a quieter residential character.
- **Remote-work fit:** excellent for staying home and working online.
- **Trade-off:** at **€1,700**, it exceeds your budget, so it only works if you can stretch or negotiate.

### 4) Alfama — Lowest Remote-Work Fit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wifi-off.svg
- **Why it’s weaker:** the older building and **20 Mbps** listing are the biggest red flags for remote work.
- **Remote-work fit:** beautiful area, but typically less practical for quiet, stable workdays.
- **Trade-off:** best for atmosphere, not for productivity.

## What to Ask Before Signing

- **Internet proof:** Is the connection fiber, and can they share a recent speed test screenshot or provider name?
- **Actual monthly cost:** What is included in rent — condo fees, water, electricity, gas, internet, and heating/cooling?
- **Noise level:** Is the apartment facing a main street, bars, schools, or a busy courtyard?
- **Building condition:** Any issues with insulation, humidity, mold, hot water, or elevator reliability?
- **Coworking access:** Which coworking spaces are nearby, and how long is the walk to the nearest metro station?
- **Lease terms:** Minimum stay, deposit amount, early termination rules, and whether registration is allowed for residency paperwork.
- **Furnishing and workspace:** Is there a proper desk, ergonomic chair, and enough outlets for a remote setup?
- **Internet contract details:** Who pays, what plan is installed, and can the tenant upgrade if needed?
